heroHeadline: WaPo: ICE Guards Used Chemical Agents on Detainees; ICE Pays Police $100K+ to Join 287(g); Mesa Gateway Overcrowded
heroSubtitle: A Washington Post investigation published May 4 found ICE guards deployed chemical agents (pepper balls) and physical force on civil immigration detainees at multiple facilities, including a case at an Alaska facility. That same day, the federal government moved to dismiss the Hussen v. Noem class action challenging Minneapolis ICE racial profiling. On May 5, NPR revealed ICE is offering local police departments $100,000+ in vehicles and equipment as financial incentives to sign 287(g) agreements — advocates called it a 'bounty system'; a Marketplace investigation found ICE using the military contracting tool WEXMAC to convert buildings into detention centers in Maryland, Michigan, and Pennsylvania, bypassing public input. On May 6, Mesa Gateway Airport Authority reported overcrowding at the adjacent ICE facility. These developments follow the House passage of the $70B enforcement package (April 30) and continue the record FY2026 pace of 30+ in-custody deaths.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, court records, and Congressional records
